text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- The justice ministry is considering introducing legislation to make it an offence to publish on the internet such things as instructions for producing bombs or drugs.
---The consumer council has warned against insurance adviser Fuld Valuta which it says charges "horrifying" fees for information that is for the most part available free elsewhere.

---Competition authorities are considering taqking action against Tele Danmark and Sonofon's practice of giving heft discounts to new subscribers. The authorities fear that customers are lured into long-term contracts to the detriment of competition.
--- Danish state railways and biotech firm Novo Nordisk are taking part in trials of plant fibre as a substitute for plastic, testing the material in train seats.

--- Danes bought 442,000 home computers in 1996, 13 percent more than the year before, but sales growth is flattening as more and more Danes -- 45 percent of the population of five million -- now have computers at home.
--- Small garages cannot afford the equipment needed to service today's technologically advanced cars and about 1,000 small garages have closed in thew past three years as a consequence.
--- A new survey shows that 95 percent of Danes are happy in their work, but at the same time 25 percent feel stressed.
---Danish firm Mobile Media reports strong interest in its offer to supply institutions with free mini-busses if they carry advertising on their sides.
---Ninety percent of fraud against Danish companies is committed by their own employees, compared with a global average of 78 percent, a suvery by accountants Ernst & Young shows.

---The Danish metalworkers' union is mobilising to encourage investors to take up an offer of 27 percent in restructured shipbuilder Danyard. If Danes do not exploit offer the holding will be taken up by Malaysian firm Penang Shipbuilding Construction, which has just announced the purchase of 48 percent of Danyard.
